title: Branch and loop in x86-64 assembly
brief: Write max, abs, clamp, a summing loop, and a bit-counting loop in assembly, and see signed and unsigned comparisons disagree.
hints: The first integer argument arrives in rdi (edi for 32 bits), the second in rsi, the third in rdx, and the result goes in rax.
`cmp a, b` computes a - b, throws the answer away, and keeps the flags. The instruction after it reads those flags: `jl`, `jg`, `jz`, `cmovl`, `setl`.
`cmovl eax, esi` copies esi into eax only when the last compare said signed less-than. It needs no jump and no label.
`setl al` writes only the low byte of rax. Clear the whole register first with `xor eax, eax`, and do it before the `cmp`, because `xor` changes the flags.
A loop is a label, a body, a `cmp`, and a conditional jump back to the label. Write local labels as `.Lloop` and `.Ldone` so they stay private.
Signed less-than is `l` (or `jl`, `setl`, `cmovl`). Unsigned less-than is `b`, for below (`jb`, `setb`, `cmovb`).
